title: World War 3 WON'T Happen. Here's why.
summary: A commentary arguing World War 3 is far less likely than social media suggests, citing nuclear deterrence, economic costs and the decline of wars between states.

assertions.quote: World War is a lot less likely than your screen is telling you.

verdicts.note: Forecasters put great-power war in the next few years well below even odds, while feeds amplify alarming content.

The US public's median forecast of a 10-million-death nuclear catastrophe by 2045 was 10%, against 5% for experts and 1% for superforecasters, so public perception runs above expert forecasts; social media itself is not measured.

assertions.quote: Interstate wars, meaning actual wars between nations, have been in long-term decline since 1945.

verdicts.note: Apart from US-Chinese fighting in Korea, no great powers have fought each other directly since 1945, and forecasters put the yearly chance in low single digits.

assertions.quote: The deterrence framework has held for 80 years not because world leaders are good people

verdicts.note: No great-power war since 1945 fits deterrence, but trade, institutions and US primacy also contributed, and it cannot be proven.

assertions.quote: Both countries lose more than they could possibly gain.

verdicts.note: Trade raises the cost of war, but the evidence is mixed: dense trade did not prevent 1914, and US-China decoupling is reducing the tie.

assertions.quote: Now, let's put aside the fact that if someone fired a nuke, it would be intercepted.

verdicts.note: Missile defences are tested against a few missiles, succeed about half the time and cannot stop a large attack.
US intelligence expects threats to the homeland to grow from over 3,000 to more than 16,000 missiles by 2035, and rivals pairing missiles with cheap expendable systems to stress US missile defences.
The Bulletin states missile defence systems are at best only partially effective and expects Golden Dome to give little real defence.

assertions.quote: if any of these systems intercepted something like a nuke, do you really think the government would tell you or really anyone about it?

verdicts.note: There is no evidence any nuclear-armed missile has been fired at a state, and a launch would be seen by many countries' early-warning satellites.

assertions.quote: The UN, with all its flaws, exists and actually mediates conflicts before they escalate, most of the time.

verdicts.note: UN mediation has helped end some wars, but the Security Council is deadlocked where great powers are involved.

assertions.quote: The risk isn't World War III. It's that enough people believe it's inevitable that they stop caring about preventing it.

verdicts.note: A claim about public attitudes with no measurable link to war risk.

The case file says a general fatalism about an eventual European war, together with Russia's rise, encouraged an aggressive attitude among German leaders who favoured preventive war before 1914. It is a historical illustration, not a measured effect.

Hanania argues that presenting US-China rivalry as fated by history has given rhetorical and political ammunition to advocates of confrontation, and that nearly every prominent analyst who accepted the framing called for more confrontational policies. This is an argument, not a measurement.
